rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains أن as expressing the sense ‘what prevents us from not fighting’; its presence is meaningful, unlike the other verse’s omission.
rows.anchor:
لما تضمنت معنى (ما) وسقوطها في الموضع الآخر على الأصل، كأنه قال: ما لنا غير مقاتلين كقوله: (فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين (49)
عن الفراء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats أن as extra, but the author rejects this because the particle has a sound meaning and need not be declared redundant.
rows.anchor: (أن) زائدة عند الأخفش، وليس بالوجه؛ لأنه لا يحكم بالزيادة، وله معنى يحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed ellipsis of واو before أن is rejected because ellipsis is unnecessary and has an available alternative.
rows.anchor: الثالث: على حذف الواو كأنه قيل: وما لنا، وأن لا نقاتل كما يقال

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another analysis takes ما as a negation, ‘why should we abandon fighting’; on the first analysis it is interrogative.
rows.anchor: الرابع: (ما) بمعنى الجحد، كأنه قيل: ما لنا نترك القتال، وعلى الوجه الأول (ما) استفهام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads قليلا in the accusative; nominative is unavailable because this is an exception after an affirmative statement.
rows.anchor: قليلا نصبا، ولا يجوز فيه الرفع؛ لأنه استثناء موجب، عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After exhorting jihad, the commentary turns to Israel’s famous refusal to fight as a warning against following their example.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم الحث على الجهاد عقبه بقصة كانت مشهورة في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألم تر means ‘do you not know,’ addressed to Muhammad; another formulation addresses the listener.
rows.anchor: ألم تر ألم تعلم يا محمد، وقيل: أيها السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ملأ are the distinguished nobles among the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: إلى الملأ جماعة الأشراف من بني إسرائيل من بعد موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘After Moses’ means after his death.
rows.anchor: من بعد موسى أي من بعد موته إذ قالوا لنبي لهم أي لرسول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the prophet they addressed as Joshua son of Nun, son of Ephraim son of Joseph.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو: يوشع بن نون بن إفرائيم بن يوسف، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the prophet as Shimʿon and explains his name through his mother’s answered prayer; the sīn became shīn in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: والسين يصير شينا بالعبرانية، وهو من ولد لاوي بن يعقوب، عن السدي

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb identifies him as Ishmuel, descended from Aaron; the author notes this is the majority exegetical view.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو إشمويل من ولد هارون، عن وهب، وعليه أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: وهب والربيع
rows.claim: Wahb and al-Rabīʿ say they sought a king to support them against the tyrannical rulers of their time.
rows.anchor: قيل: استدلال عن الجبابرة لهم من الملوك الذين كانوا في زمانهم، عن وهب والربيع

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says their request was to fight the Amalekites.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قتال العمالقة، عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Jalut’s people had overrun Israel, enslaving their children and killing their fighters, so they wanted a king to unite them for war.
rows.anchor: تغلب قوم جالوت على بني إسرائيل فسبوا ذراريهم، وقتل مقاتلتهم ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel’s polity depended on a king to lead warfare and administer judgments and a prophet whom the king obeyed to maintain religion and convey revelation.
rows.anchor: وكان قوام أمر بني إسرائيل بملك يجتمعون عليه لجهاد الأعداء ويجري الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Fighting in God’s path’ means fighting for His religion and against His enemies.
rows.anchor: نقاتل نحارب في سبيل الله في سبيل دينه وجهاد أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل عسيتم means ‘perhaps’; the prophet asks whether, if fighting is imposed, they will fail to fulfill it and fight alongside the king.
rows.anchor: فقال تعالى: (هل عسيتم) أي لعلكم (إن كتب عليكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nobles answer that they should fight because they and their families were driven from their homes; the wording is general but refers to some of them.
rows.anchor: قالوا يعني الملأ وما لنا ألا نقاتل في سبيل الله وقد أخرجنا لفظه عام ومعناه خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account leaves implicit that God granted their request and imposed fighting; they then turned away, except the few who crossed the river.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام محذوف تقديره: فسأل الله تعالى ذلك فبعث لهم ملكا، وكتب عليهم القتال فتولوا

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the wrongdoers are those who disobey God’s commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: يعني من لم يطعه في أمره ونهيه، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they are those who abandon jihad after it becomes obligatory.
rows.anchor: عليم بمن ترك الجهاد بعد وجوبه، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people protected worldly interests while neglecting religion, which prompted their objection; the excerpt ends before completing the point.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن القوم حافظوا على أمر الدنيا، وتركوا أمر الدين؛ لذلك أنكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the warning generally: do not abandon the commanded direction toward the Kaʿba and thereby give anyone an argument against you.
rows.anchor: على العموم (عليكم حجة) يعني: لا تعدلوا عما أمركم الله به من التوجه إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation says the change prevents the People of the Book from arguing that Muslims contradicted the scriptural prediction of prayer toward the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: لئلا يكون لأهل الكتاب عليكم حجة لو جاء على خلاف ما تقدمت به البشارة في الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews said Muhammad did not know the qibla until they guided him; Quraysh said he had abandoned Abraham’s qibla.
rows.anchor: أما اليهود فيقولون: ما درى محمد أين قبلته حتى هديناهم

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: One view takes the wrongdoers as Jews and Quraysh: Quraysh say he returned to his forefathers’ qibla and will return to their religion, while Jews say the change was his own uninformed judgment.
rows.anchor: أما قريش فقالوا: إنه علم أنه قبلة آبائه فرجع إليه، وسيرجع إلى ديننا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والربيع والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and al-Suddī identify the People of the Book as the people generally and Meccan polytheists as the wrongdoers, who allege Muhammad is confused and will return to their religion.
rows.anchor: إن محمدا تحير في دينه فتوجه إلى قبلتنا، وسيرجع إلى ديننا، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والربيع والسدي

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: A general interpretation identifies the wrongdoers as those who wronged the Muslims through retaliation and refusal to listen.
rows.anchor: هو على العموم، والذين ظلموا يعني ظلموكم بالمقابلة وقلة الاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed identifications depend on whether the exception is treated as connected or disconnected; Abū ʿUbayda and Quṭrub take another analysis.
rows.anchor: هذه الأقوال على قول من يقول: إنه استثناء صحيح أو منقطع

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: One explanation addresses Muslims: do not fear the disputants, who have no proof or power over you; fear God by keeping Islam and the Kaʿba direction.
rows.anchor: خطاب للمسلمين لئلا يخافوا من تقدم ذكره من المتعنتين

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another reading warns against committing sins out of fear of others and promises that God will suffice against them.
rows.anchor: لأجل خشيتكم من الغير، لا تركبوا المعاصي واخشون بتركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the earlier purpose clause: fear God rather than people so that the religious and worldly blessing may be completed.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله: لئلا، وتقديره: لئلا يكون لأحد عليكم حجة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says the completed blessing is guidance to the Kaʿba, the qibla of the prophets; the change restored the Muslims’ former standing, and the Prophet had wanted it.
rows.anchor: فهذا تمام النعمة، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajh is a thing’s front or what faces another; it can mean a person’s face, an evident aspect, or the thing itself.
rows.anchor: الوجه: مستقبل كل شيء، والوجاه والتجاه: ما استقبل شيء شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam linguistically means submission and compliance; in religious usage Islam and faith are one, and aslama can mean handing over or becoming sincere.
rows.anchor: والإسلام في اللغة: الاستسلام، وهو الانقياد، وفي الشرع الإيمان والإسلام واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلى can answer an implied question about whether anyone enters paradise, inferred from the preceding discussion, or rebut an assertion of negation.
rows.anchor: فأما ههنا فدخلت على تقدير: أما يدخل الجنة أحد؟ فقيل: بلى من أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is that بلى answers the preceding denial, as in the example ‘Zayd did not stand; yes, he did.’
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون جوابا للحجة على التكذيب، كقولك: ما قام زيد، فيقول: بلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وهو محسن is a circumstantial clause, with the waw marking the circumstance and the sense ‘while doing good.’
rows.anchor: وموضع وهو محسن نصب على الحال كأنه قيل: محسنا، والواو واو الحال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, and Muqātil take it to mean surrendering oneself to God by following what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: أسلم نفسه لله، بأن سلك طريق مرضاته، عن ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets ‘his face’ as the direction of his religious commitment.
rows.anchor: وجهه يعني: وجهه في الدين، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Other explanations say that he directs himself to God’s obedience, is sincere, or submits humbly to God’s command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استسلم لأمر الله وخضع له وتواضع

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: محسن is interpreted as a believer, one who does good deeds, or one who is sincere.
rows.anchor: محسن في أعماله، وقيل: مخلص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His reward is the recompense for his deeds.
rows.anchor: فله أجره يعني: جزاء عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular form agrees with من grammatically even though its meaning is plural, which explains the later plural pronoun عليهم.
rows.anchor: لأن (من) لفظها لفظ الواحد، ومعناه معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing monotheism and the reward and punishment of its adherents and opponents, the commentary recalls God’s favors to both groups and warns against following Satan as ingratitude.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى التوحيد وما لأهله من الثواب وذكر الشرك وما لأهله من العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address ‘O people’ is general, directed to all accountable descendants of Adam.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الناس وهذا خطاب عام لجميع المكلفين من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative ‘eat’ expresses permission; the following qualification distinguishes what is lawful and wholesome from forbidden food.
rows.anchor: كلوا صيغته أمر، ومعناه الإباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification matters because some food is forbidden and some permitted: the former brings ruin while the latter strengthens worship.
rows.anchor: والأول يعقب الهلكة، والثاني يقوي على العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يُتوفون means they are taken or die; يذرون أزواجا means they leave wives, understood as women who were their wives even if now unrelated.
rows.anchor: أي يقبضون ويموتون ويذرون أزواجا أي يتركون أزواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The widows wait until the waiting period ends before marriage and keep themselves in widowhood during that time.
rows.anchor: (يتربصن) أي ينتظرن انقضاء العدة للوصول إلى النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The period is four months and ten days; one report explains ‘ten’ as ten nights and days because the husband remains in the body during them.
rows.anchor: أربعة أشهر وعشرا يعني عشر ليال وعشرة أيام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib is cited for the explanation that the husband remains in the body during the ten-day period.
rows.anchor: لأن الزوج يمسك في الجسد فيها، عن سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the appointed term means that the waiting period has ended.
rows.anchor: فإذا بلغن أجلهن يعني آخر العدة بانقضائها

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: One view takes the address as the guardians, who arrange the marriage contract; another takes it as everyone, who must prevent marriage during the waiting period.
rows.anchor: خطاب للأولياء؛ لأنه يتولى العقد، وقيل: للجميع لأنه يلزمهم منعها

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: A further parsing understands the phrase as removing blame from the women and others for her marriage and adornment after the waiting period.
rows.anchor: تقديره لا جناح عليكم يعني على النساء وعليكم فيما فعلن في أنفسهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their deeds, so they should avoid disobeying His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والله بما تعملون خبير عليم بأعمالهم فاجتنبوا مخالفة أمره ونهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A waiting period is obligatory after a husband’s death whether the marriage was consummated or not, unlike a divorce waiting period; the verse’s wording is general.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوبها سواء دخل بها أم لم يدخل بخلاف عدة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The widow’s term is four months and ten days except for pregnant women, whose term ends at childbirth; the author says this is the jurists’ consensus.
rows.anchor: فقيل: عدتها بوضع الحمل دون الأشهر لظاهر قوله: (وأولات الأحمال)

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed Subayʿa bt. al-Ḥārith, who gave birth days after her husband died, that she could marry.
rows.anchor: النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أمر سبيعة بنت الحارث، وكانت وضعت

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar said that if she delivered while her husband lay on his bier, her waiting period would have ended.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر: لو وضعت ما في بطنها وزوجها على سريره

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود البدري وأبو هريرة وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, Abū Hurayra, and Ibn Masʿūd are also cited for ending the pregnant widow’s term at delivery; Ibn Masʿūd challenged others that the short women’s sūra came after the Baqara verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: من شاء باهلته أن سورة النساء القصرى نزلت بعد الآية في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī and a group hold that a pregnant widow waits for whichever is later: childbirth or the four months and ten days.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن عدتها أبعد الأجلين عن علي (عليه السلام) وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the disbelievers desist, they have stopped their unbelief through repentance; God covers their sins and rewards them in paradise.
rows.anchor: فإن انتهوا امتنعوا عن كفرهم بالتوبة فإن الله غفور رحيم

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: An alternative supplies omitted words: if they desist by repenting, God forgives them because He is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فيه حذف، وتقديره: فإن انتهوا بالتوبة، فإن الله يغفر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fighting is obligatory only while they persist in unbelief and is forbidden once they desist.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على أن قتالهم يجب بشرط إقامتهم على الكفر، وأنه محظور إذا انتهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that repentance is accepted from every sin, including the greatest sin of unbelief, refuting the claim that a murderer cannot repent.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن التوبة مقبولة من كل ذنب؛ لأن الكفر أعظم الذنوب، فيبطل قول من يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the claim that a repentant person needs no forgiveness and only a persistent sinner needs it, since forgiveness follows their desistance.
rows.anchor: وتدل على بطلان القول بأن التائب لا يحتاج إلى مغفرة، وإنما يحتاج إليها المصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUdwan literally means exceeding the limit; here it figuratively means requital for wrongdoing, as in calling requital for an evil ‘an evil.’
rows.anchor: العدوان: أصله مجاوزة الحد، وهو هاهنا توسع ومجاز، وتقديره: فلا نحب جزاء العدوان

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says fitna here means unbelief because it leads to destruction, as a trial does.
rows.anchor: والفتنة: الكفر ههنا سمي بذلك؛ لأنه يؤدي إلى الهلاك، كما تؤدي إليه الفتنة، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation derives fitna from corruption becoming manifest during a test.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه أظهر الفساد عند الاختبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn can mean custom, obedience, or the religion one follows.
rows.anchor: والدين: العادة، والدين: الطاعة، والدين: ما يتدين به

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع وعكرمة
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and ʿIkrima take the goal as ending polytheism among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: على المشركين، عن قتادة والربيع وعكرمة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads the goal as ending warfare, so they stop fighting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا تكون حرب فتركوا القتال، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the phrase obedience and submission to God’s command.
rows.anchor: ويكون الدين لله الطاعة والانقياد لأمره

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation says Islam should prevail over all religions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يكون الدين دين الإسلام فيظهر على جميع الأديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘no aggression’ means there is no recourse or requital except against wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فلا عدوان أي: لا سبيل ولا جزاء إلا على الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that fighting is obligatory.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على وجوب القتال

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī considers the verse abrogating earlier limits because it commands fighting even if the opponents did not initiate, to eliminate unbelief.
rows.anchor: إنها ناسخة لما قبلها؛ لأنه أمر بالقتال، وإن لم يبدؤوا لكيلا يكون كفر، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another view says it is not abrogated: if they initiate fighting in the sanctuary, Muslims must fight until unbelief disappears.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليس بمنسوخ، ولكن إذا ابتدؤوا بالقتال في الحرم يجب مقاتلتهم

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: A third view treats the verse as confirmation of what came before.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو تأكيد لما تقدم

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: A fragment reports a view attributed to Shurayḥ that the amount is five hundred dirhams; the preceding limit is truncated in the excerpt.
rows.anchor:
درهم، عن شريح.
(وإن طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads النصف with ḍamma on the nūn; both vocalizations are recognized dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة فنصف بكسر النون، وعن السلمي بضمها، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads يعفو with a still wāw to avoid the vowel on wāw; the common reading has fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويعفو بسكون الواو استثقالا للفتحة على الواو

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reads وإن يعفوا with masculine plural yāʾ agreement referring to the person who holds the marriage bond; the common reading addresses the audience with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي، وإن يعفوا بالياء خبرا عن (الذي بيده عقدة النكاح)، وقراءة العامة بالتاء على الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has ولا تنسوا without an alif and with ḍamma on wāw.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة ولا تنسوا بغير ألف، وضم الواو

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reads تناسوا with an added alif as a reciprocal form.
rows.anchor: وعن علي (عليه السلام) تناسوا بالألف من المفاعلة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar reads without the alif and with kasra on wāw.
rows.anchor: وعن يحيى بن يعمر بغير ألف وكسر الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The half is one of two equal parts; an indivisible part cannot itself have a half because it is not made of two parts.
rows.anchor: وهو: جزء من اثنين على المساواة، والجزء الذي لا يتجزأ ليس له نصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAfw means leaving or letting go; divine pardon leaves deserved punishment uninflicted, and surplus wealth is what remains after spending.
rows.anchor: والعفو: الترك، وعفو الله تعالى عن خلقه معناه استحقوا العقوبة فترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisyān can mean either forgetting or leaving, as in the statement that they forgot God and He forgot them.
rows.anchor: والنسيان: خلاف الذكر، والنسيان الترك، ومنه: (نسوا الله فنسيهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasʾ means delay, as in the Qurʾānic term al-nasīʾ and the word nasīʾa.
rows.anchor: والنسأ: التأخير، ومنه: (إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر) ومنه النسيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḍl means increase or goodness; ifḍāl means beneficence, while mutafaḍḍil describes one claiming superiority over peers.
rows.anchor: والفضل: الزيادة والخير، والإفضال: الإحسان، والمتفضل: المدعي للفضل على أقرانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فنصف is nominative with an implied عليكم, ‘upon you is half’; another construction supplies an imperative, ‘give half.’
rows.anchor: رفع (فنصف) بتقدير فعليكم نصف ما فرضتم، ويجوز في العربية النصف أي أدوا نصف ما فرضتم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb with tāʾ, addressing the Prophet: ‘if you saw.’
rows.anchor: ولو ترى يا محمد، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another reading takes the Prophet as the grammatical addressee while intending others, as in the address to the Prophet followed by ‘you divorced’ in 65:1.
rows.anchor: والمراد غيره كقوله: الذين آمنوا (ياأيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء)

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: The tāʾ form may instead address any listener or person generally.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولو ترى أيها السامع أو أيها الإنسان فالخطاب لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With yāʾ, the subject is the wrongdoer himself: ‘if this wrongdoer saw.’
rows.anchor: وأما الياء فالمراد نفس الذين ظلموا تقديره: ولو يرى هذا الظالم

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Vision is interpreted either as physically seeing or as knowing.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في الرؤية، فقيل: لو يبصرون، وقيل: لو يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the visual reading, seeing how people dispute at the punishment would astonish the viewer; on the knowledge reading, the wrongdoers would not have supported injustice if they knew.
rows.anchor: لو رأيتهم عند رؤية العذاب كيف يتجادلون لعجبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis supplies ‘they know’ before أن القوة لله, connecting the clause to what precedes.
rows.anchor: فيه حذف كأنه قيل: يعلمون أن القوة لله، فعلى هذا يتصل بما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the clause independent, with an understood ‘they saw’ and their deeds and bad outcome preceding it.
rows.anchor: أن القوة مستأنف والحذف ل (رأوا) - مضمرة - فعلهم وسوء عاقبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power means He can seize and punish them; their idols and mutual support cannot help them.
rows.anchor: أن القوة لله يعني هو قادر على أخذهم وعقوبتهم، وفيه وعيد

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation says all power comes from God, who creates it in people; they should not worship idols that possess no power, benefit, or harm.
rows.anchor: إن القوة كلها من الله خلقها في العباد فكيف يعبد بها سواه من الأنداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the punishment severe intensifies the description; this is figurative because severity properly belongs to bodies.
rows.anchor: وصف العذاب بالشدة مبالغة في الوصف، وهو توسع؛ لأن الشدة من صفات الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers love God, His worship, and jihad enough to sacrifice themselves and their wealth for Him.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن المؤمن يحب الله تعالى، ويحب عبادته والجهاد في سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know God best love Him most; the author argues this is the people of divine unity and justice because they know God as just and beneficent, creator of them for paradise, and one who does not wrong or create anyone for hell.
rows.anchor: أشد الناس حبا لله أعرفهم به، فتدل من هذا الوجه أنه ليس في المكلفين أشد حبا لله من أهل التوحيد والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhfīf is the opposite of intensification; lightness and heaviness are literal in bodies and extended figuratively to other things.
rows.anchor: والتخفيف: خلاف التثقيل، وأصله الخفة، والثقل حقيقة في الأجسام

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the terms ultimately refer to component parts.
rows.anchor: يرجعان إلى الأجزاء، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abū Hāshim says the terms ultimately refer to reliance or pressure.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى الاعتماد، عن أبي هاشم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاتباع is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: ‘its ruling is following the injured party’s claim,’ or ‘then upon him is following it.’
rows.anchor: فاتباع رفع لأنه خبر ابتداء محذوف، وتقديره: فحكمه اتباع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that two Arab clans fought before Islam; the stronger clan took women without dowry and demanded disproportionate revenge, including a free man for a slave and two men for one.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أن حيين من العرب اقتتلوا قبل الإسلام، فكان بينهم قتل وجراحات

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse concerned two groups, one Muslim and one protected non-Muslim, who fought during the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي أنها نزلت في قومين أحدهما: مسلم، والآخر معاهد

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another view says the verse was revealed about two clans of the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في حيين من الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse moves from the general conditions of righteousness to individual laws, beginning with retaliation for blood and wounds because it is especially important; كتب means ‘made obligatory.’
rows.anchor: بدأ بذكر القصاص في الدماء والجراح؛ لأنه أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording signals obligation twice: كتب is used for legal duties, and عليكم expresses something binding upon the addressee.
rows.anchor: هذه اللفظة تقتضي الوجوب من وجهين: أحدهما: قوله: (كتب)

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation says the duty of retaliation was written for them in the Preserved Record.
rows.anchor: معنى (كتب) أن هذا الوجوب كتب عليهم في أم الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiṣāṣ means equivalence: the killer receives the same treatment as the slain person.
rows.anchor: القصاص يعني المساواة، فيفعل بالقاتل مثل ما فعله بالمقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text asks how retaliation can be obligatory when the heirs may choose or waive it and the person punished does not perform it; it distinguishes two answers about who bears the duty.
rows.anchor: كيف يجب القصاص مع تخيير الأولياء، فإنه مخير بين فعله وتركه

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: One answer says retaliation becomes obligatory if the heir chooses it.
rows.anchor: الأول: فرض ذلك إن اختار الولي القصاص

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another answer says what is obligatory is to keep within the prescribed limit and not exceed it.
rows.anchor: كتب عليكم التمسك بما حد لكم دون التعدي فيما ليس لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage treats childbirth as the waiting term across divorced and widowed women, women counting qurūʾ, and free and enslaved women; a divorced woman whose marriage was not consummated has no waiting period.
rows.anchor: وضع الحمل ففي الجميع على السواء المطلقة المتوفى عنها زوجها، وذوات الأقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting period combines God’s right with a human right and is partly devotional: abstaining from marriage, residence, and mourning are devotional, but elapsed time is not.
rows.anchor: والعدة حق الله تعالى مشوب بحق الآدمي، وتعبد للمرأة من وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a woman learns of the divorce only after time has passed, the jurists agree that the period starts at divorce; some instead count from when she receives the news.
rows.anchor: فالفقهاء على أنه يعتبر من حين الطلاق، وعن بعضهم من حين الخبر، والأول إجماع الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revocation applies to a revocable one- or twofold divorce, not a threefold divorce, a kināya divorce, or a divorce for consideration; al-Shāfiʿī allows it in kināya as well.
rows.anchor: فتثبت في المطلقة الرجعية في الواحدة والثنتين، وتبين في الثلاث، وفي الكنايات لا تثبت الرجعة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa counts intercourse or lustful touching as a return to the marriage; al-Shāfiʿī does not accept return by those acts.
rows.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة يصير به مراجعا، وعند الشافعي لا تصح الرجعة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says witnesses are not a condition for revocation; al-Shāfiʿī says they are.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فقال أبو حنيفة: الإشهاد ليس بشرط، وقال الشافعي: شرط

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: All agree the right of return ends when the waiting period ends; Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad accept a return announced during menstruation if she says the period ended.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أنه إذا انقضت العدة تنقطع الرجعة، فأما في الحيض إذا قال: راجعتك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa rejects that return when the menstrual period lasted ten days, because the right ends as soon as menstruation stops.
rows.anchor: لا تصح عند أبي حنيفة إذا كان حيضها عشرا، فبنفس الانقطاع تنقطع الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage exposes and warns against the hypocrites’ obstinate rejection: they knew the truth but abandoned it, and its disclosure of their secrets is a sign of the Prophet’s miracle.
rows.anchor: معاندين، علموا الحق وتركوه، وتدل على معجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading uses third-person yāʾ; some read with second-person tāʾ addressing the hearers.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة يسرون ويعلنون بالياء، وعن بعضهم بالتاء على المخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿlān means making something manifest or perceptible; it is the opposite of concealment, isrār.
rows.anchor: الإعلان: الإظهار، وهو إخراج الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial hamza is interrogative with a reproachful force, as in the cited question ‘How can you disbelieve in God?’
rows.anchor: الألف في قوله: أولا يعلمون ألف استفهام صارت بمعنى التوبيخ

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the ones who should know as the Jews; Abū ʿAlī says they are the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أولا يعلمون يعني اليهود عن أكثر المفسرين، وقيل: يعني المنافقين، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and others say God knows their concealed rejection of Muhammad and their public profession to believers that they have faith.
rows.anchor: من كفرهم بمحمد وما يعلنون يظهرون للمؤمنين من قولهم: إنا آمنا، عن الحسن وقتادة وجماعة

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Muslim take the words generally: God knows everything people hide and make public.
rows.anchor: يعلم جميع ما يسرون وما يعلنون، عن أبي علي وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation asks whether they do not know that their deceptions cannot fool one who knows private and public matters.
rows.anchor: أولا يعلمون أن مثل هذه المخاريق لا تروج على من يعلم السر والعلانية

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says they should have known from the signs and proofs God established that He knows their private and public affairs.
rows.anchor: بالآيات والدلالة التي أقامها الله تعالى، أن الله يعلم سرهم وعلانيتهم، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they should know that the God they already acknowledge knows their secrets and what they make public, showing that they recognized God.
rows.anchor: الله الذي أقروا به يعلم سرهم وجهرهم، عن أبي علي، وهذا يدل على أنهم كانوا عالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhḏ means the opposite of giving, and mīthāq is a strengthened covenant; ashraba can mean watering a crop or making a color adhere, and the idiom describes love entering the heart.
rows.anchor: الأخذ: نقيض الإعطاء. والميثاق: العهد المؤكد

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s verse ‘love drank it’ illustrates the idiom that love has become deeply rooted in someone’s heart.
rows.anchor: قال زهير: فصحوت عنها بعد حب داخل ... والحب تشربه فؤادك داء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of the covenant and mountain is another reproach over Israel’s ancestors and their rejection of the commands.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى خصلة أخرى من أسلافهم توبيخا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant means they accepted the command, and al-Ṭūr is the mountain raised over them, explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وقبلتم الأمر، فأخذنا ذلك عليكم، ورفعنا فوقكم الطور، يعني الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition elsewhere emphasizes the argument against the opponent in the customary style of Arab address.
rows.anchor: والتكرار في هذا وأمثاله للتأكيد، وإيجاب الحجة على الخصم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the argument is repeated because the Jews renewed their claim to be God’s children and beloved; circumstances differ, so it is not redundant.
rows.anchor: عن أبي علي، كأنه يشير إلى اختلاف الأحوال والأوقات

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Another explanation says that recounting Israel’s offenses required repeating the mountain and their response, ‘we heard and disobeyed.’
rows.anchor: لما عد فضائح اليهود أعاد ذكر رفع الجبل، وقولهم: (سمعنا وعصينا)

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: ‘What We gave you’ is identified either as the Torah or as the religious laws.
rows.anchor: خذوا ما آتيناكم أي أعطيناكم، قيل: التوراة، وقيل: الشرائع

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: Bi-quwwa means serious effort and diligence, or the ability they possess to take up the command.
rows.anchor: بقوة قيل: بجد واجتهاد، وقيل: بقدرة، أي وأنتم قادرون على أخذه

rows.speaker: unspecified
rows.claim: ‘Listen’ may mean accept what you have heard, or listen attentively to what is recited; the author says the two senses can coexist.
rows.anchor: قيل: اقبلوا ما سمعتم، كقوله: سمع الله لمن حمده، أي قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording permits both listening and acceptance, and may be understood to require first listening and then obeying.
rows.anchor: وهذا اللفظ يحتمل الاستماع والقبول، ولا تنافي بينهما

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz verse about hearing, obeying, and submitting supports the sense of listening as accepting and complying.
rows.anchor: قال الراجز: السمع والطاعة والتسليم ... خير وأعفى لبني تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they literally said ‘we hear you but disobey your command’ mockingly, which was unbelief.
rows.anchor: قالوه استهزاء: سمعنا قولك، وعصينا أمرك، وذلك كفر
